ko.title: [소비자 심리학 #11] 왜 $19.99는 $20보다 싸게 느껴질까: 가격의 심리학

segments.src: > A price is never judged alone. We compare it to a number in our heads, read it from left to right, and react to how a discount is framed, so the same dollar amount can feel like a bargain or a rip-off.
segments.tr: > 가격은 결코 혼자서 판단되지 않습니다. 우리는 머릿속의 숫자와 비교하고, 왼쪽에서 오른쪽으로 읽으며, 할인이 어떻게 제시되는지에 반응합니다. 그래서 같은 금액이라도 득템으로 느껴지거나 바가지로 느껴질 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Economics textbooks often treat price as a simple fact: a product costs $20, and you decide whether it is worth $20 to you.
segments.tr: 경제학 교과서는 흔히 가격을 단순한 사실로 다룹니다. 제품이 $20이고, 여러분은 그것이 나에게 $20의 가치가 있는지 결정한다는 식입니다.

segments.src: Real shoppers don't work that way.
segments.tr: 실제 소비자는 그렇게 판단하지 않습니다.

segments.src: Consumer psychology shows that people judge prices **relative to something else**, and that small details in how a price is shown can change how it feels.
segments.tr: 소비자 심리학에 따르면 사람들은 가격을 **다른 무언가와 비교하여** 판단하며, 가격이 제시되는 방식의 작은 세부 요소도 가격이 주는 느낌을 바꿀 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Three ideas explain most of this.
segments.tr: 이를 설명하는 핵심 아이디어는 세 가지입니다.

segments.src: Reference price: "Compared to what?"**
segments.tr: 기준 가격: "무엇과 비교하는가?"**

segments.src: A reference price is the benchmark you use to decide whether a price is high or low.
segments.tr: 기준 가격이란 어떤 가격이 비싼지 싼지를 판단할 때 사용하는 기준점입니다.

segments.src: It comes from two places:
segments.tr: 기준 가격은 두 가지 출처에서 생깁니다:

segments.src: - **Internal reference price** is the number already in your memory: what you paid last time, what you think is "normal," what a friend said they paid.
segments.tr: - **내부 기준 가격**은 이미 여러분의 기억 속에 있는 숫자입니다. 지난번에 지불한 금액, "보통"이라고 생각하는 가격, 친구가 샀다고 말한 가격 등이 여기에 해당합니다.

segments.src: - **External reference price** is a number the seller shows you: a "Was $80" tag, a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP), or a pricier item placed right next to the one being sold.
segments.tr: - **외부 기준 가격**은 판매자가 보여주는 숫자입니다. "Was $80" 표시, 제조사 권장 소비자가격(MSRP), 또는 판매 중인 제품 바로 옆에 놓인 더 비싼 제품 등이 해당합니다.

segments.src: A $60 jacket feels like a deal if you expected $90, and feels expensive if you expected $40.
segments.tr: $90을 예상했다면 $60짜리 재킷은 득템처럼 느껴지고, $40을 예상했다면 비싸게 느껴집니다.

segments.src: The price itself didn't change.
segments.tr: 가격 자체는 바뀌지 않았습니다.

segments.src: The comparison did.
segments.tr: 바뀐 것은 비교 대상입니다.

segments.src: This connects to *anchoring*, the tendency for the first number we see to pull later judgments toward it.
segments.tr: 이는 *앵커링*과 관련이 있습니다. 앵커링이란 처음 본 숫자가 이후의 판단을 그 숫자 쪽으로 끌어당기는 경향을 말합니다.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9: the left-digit effect**
segments.tr: 끝자리가 9인 가격: 왼쪽 자릿수 효과**

segments.src: Why do so many prices end in .99 or 9?
segments.tr: 왜 그렇게 많은 가격이 .99나 9로 끝날까요?

segments.src: One well-supported explanation is the **left-digit effect**.
segments.tr: 잘 뒷받침되는 설명 중 하나는 **왼쪽 자릿수 효과**입니다.

segments.src: We read numbers left to right, and the first digit gets more attention than the rest.
segments.tr: 우리는 숫자를 왼쪽에서 오른쪽으로 읽으며, 첫 자릿수가 나머지보다 더 많은 주의를 끕니다.

segments.src: So $19.99 tends to register as "nineteen-something," not "basically twenty," even though the difference is a single cent.
segments.tr: 그래서 $19.99는 차이가 1센트뿐인데도 "거의 20"이 아니라 "19점대"로 인식되는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: Research has found the effect is strongest when the leftmost digit changes ($2.99 vs.
segments.tr: 연구에 따르면 이 효과는 가장 왼쪽 자릿수가 바뀔 때($2.99 vs.

segments.src: $3.00), not when it stays the same ($2.89 vs.
segments.tr: $3.00) 가장 강하고, 자릿수가 같을 때($2.89 vs.
$2.90)는 약합니다.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9 also carry a second signal: many shoppers have learned to associate them with sales and discounts.
segments.tr: 끝자리가 9인 가격에는 두 번째 신호도 있습니다. 많은 소비자가 이런 가격을 세일 및 할인과 연관 짓도록 학습되어 있다는 것입니다.

segments.src: In one well-known field experiment with a women's clothing catalog, the same dress sold more at $39 than at either $34 or $44.
segments.tr: 여성복 카탈로그를 대상으로 한 잘 알려진 현장 실험에서, 같은 원피스가 $34나 $44보다 $39에 더 많이 팔렸습니다.

segments.src: The 9-ending outsold even a *lower* price.
segments.tr: 끝자리 9 가격이 *더 낮은* 가격보다도 더 많이 팔린 것입니다.

segments.src: That said, 9-endings are not magic.
segments.tr: 그렇다고 끝자리 9가 마법은 아닙니다.

segments.src: Luxury and premium brands often prefer round numbers ($200, not $199.99) precisely because round prices signal quality rather than bargain.
segments.tr: 명품 및 프리미엄 브랜드는 흔히 둥근 숫자($199.99가 아닌 $200)를 선호하는데, 둥근 가격은 할인이 아니라 품질을 나타내기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Discount perception: framing the savings**
segments.tr: 할인 인식: 절약액을 프레이밍하기**

segments.src: The same discount can be described in different ways, and the description matters.
segments.tr: 같은 할인도 다른 방식으로 표현할 수 있으며, 그 표현 방식이 중요합니다.

segments.src: - **Percent vs. dollars:** For cheaper items, a percentage often looks bigger ("25% off" a $12 item sounds better than "$3 off"). For expensive items, the dollar figure often looks bigger ("$300 off" a $1,500 laptop sounds better than "20% off"). Marketers sometimes call this the "rule of 100": below $100, show the percent; above $100, show the dollars. It's a useful rule of thumb, not a law.
segments.tr: - **퍼센트 vs. 금액:** 저렴한 상품은 퍼센트가 더 크게 보이는 경우가 많습니다($12짜리 상품의 "25% 할인"은 "$3 할인"보다 좋아 보입니다). 비싼 상품은 금액이 더 크게 보이는 경우가 많습니다($1,500짜리 노트북의 "$300 할인"은 "20% 할인"보다 좋아 보입니다). 마케터들은 이를 "100의 법칙"이라고 부르기도 합니다. 100달러 미만이면 퍼센트를, 100달러 이상이면 금액을 보여주라는 것입니다. 유용한 경험 법칙일 뿐 법칙 자체는 아닙니다.

segments.src: - **Relative savings:** People will drive across town to save $10 on a $30 item but often won't for $10 off a $1,000 item, even though the savings are identical. We tend to judge savings as a proportion of the price, not in absolute dollars.
segments.tr: - **상대적 절약:** 사람들은 $30짜리 상품에서 $10을 아끼려고 도시를 가로질러 운전해 가면서도, $1,000짜리 상품의 $10 할인에는 같은 수고를 하지 않는 경우가 많습니다. 절약액은 동일한데도 말입니다. 우리는 절약을 절대 금액이 아니라 가격에 대한 비율로 판단하는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: A famous U.S.
segments.tr: 미국의 유명한

segments.src: retail story shows how strong reference prices are.
segments.tr: 유통 사례는 기준 가격이 얼마나 강력한지 보여줍니다.

segments.src: In 2012, **JCPenney** tried to simplify its pricing.
segments.tr: 2012년 **JCPenney**는 가격 체계를 단순화하려 했습니다.

segments.src: Instead of marking items up and then running constant sales and coupons, it moved to "fair and square" everyday prices that were often similar to what shoppers had been paying after discounts anyway.
segments.tr: 제품에 가격을 올린 뒤 끊임없이 세일과 쿠폰을 진행하는 대신, "공정하고 정직한" 상시 가격으로 전환했는데, 이 가격은 할인 후 소비자들이 실제로 지불하던 가격과 비슷한 경우가 많았습니다.

segments.src: On paper, customers weren't losing money.
segments.tr: 문서상으로는 고객이 돈을 잃은 것이 없었습니다.

segments.src: But they lost the "Was $50, now $29.99" comparison, and with it the feeling of winning a deal.
segments.tr: 하지만 "Was $50, now $29.99"라는 비교와 함께 득템했다는 느낌도 사라졌습니다.

segments.src: Sales fell sharply, the CEO behind the change was replaced in 2013, and the company brought back its sales and coupons.
segments.tr: 매출은 급감했고, 이 변화를 주도했던 CEO는 2013년에 교체되었으며, 회사는 다시 세일과 쿠폰을 도입했습니다.

segments.src: You can see the same psychology on any weekend at Target, Walmart, or on Amazon: a crossed-out "List Price," a "Save 30%" badge, or a $29.99 tag sitting next to a $49.99 "premium" version.
segments.tr: 같은 심리는 주말마다 Target, Walmart, Amazon에서도 볼 수 있습니다. 취소선이 그어진 "List Price", "Save 30%" 배지, 또는 $49.99짜리 "프리미엄" 제품 옆에 놓인 $29.99 가격표 등이 그것입니다.

segments.src: Each one is designed to give you a reference point that makes the price in front of you look reasonable.
segments.tr: 이 모든 것은 눈앞의 가격이 합리적으로 보이도록 만드는 기준점을 제공하기 위해 설계된 것입니다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. We judge prices against a **reference price**, either remembered (internal) or shown by the seller (external), so context can make the same price feel cheap or expensive.
segments.tr: 1. 우리는 가격을 **기준 가격**과 비교해 판단합니다. 기준 가격은 기억에서 오는 것(내부)일 수도 있고 판매자가 보여주는 것(외부)일 수도 있으며, 따라서 같은 가격도 맥락에 따라 싸게도 비싸게도 느껴질 수 있습니다.

segments.src: 2. Prices ending in 9 work partly because of the **left-digit effect** and partly because shoppers link them with sales; round prices tend to signal quality instead.
segments.tr: 2. 끝자리가 9인 가격이 효과적인 이유는 일부는 **왼쪽 자릿수 효과** 때문이고, 일부는 소비자가 이를 세일과 연관 짓기 때문입니다. 반면 둥근 가격은 품질을 나타내는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: 3. How a **discount** is framed (percent vs. dollars, relative vs. absolute savings) changes how big it feels, even when the money saved is the same.
segments.tr: 3. **할인**을 어떻게 표현하느냐(퍼센트 vs. 금액, 상대적 vs. 절대적 절약액)에 따라, 실제 절약액이 같더라도 할인이 체감되는 크기가 달라집니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자기 점검 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** A "Was $120" tag printed next to a $79 price is an example of:
segments.tr: **Q1.** $79 가격 옆에 인쇄된 "Was $120" 표시는 다음의 예시입니다:

segments.src: - (a) Internal reference price
segments.tr: - (a) 내부 기준 가격

segments.src: - (b) External reference price
segments.tr: - (b) 외부 기준 가격

segments.src: - (c) The left-digit effect
segments.tr: - (c) 왼쪽 자릿수 효과

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X: The left-digit effect predicts that changing a price from $4.00 to $3.99 will typically feel like a bigger drop than changing it from $4.50 to $4.49.
segments.tr: **Q2.** O/X: 왼쪽 자릿수 효과에 따르면, $4.50에서 $4.49로 바꾸는 것보다 $4.00에서 $3.99로 바꾸는 것이 보통 더 큰 인하로 느껴진다.

segments.src: **Q3.** A store is discounting a $1,200 sofa by 15%.
segments.tr: **Q3.** 한 가게가 $1,200짜리 소파를 15% 할인하고 있습니다.

segments.src: Based on the "rule of 100," which framing is likely to look more attractive?
segments.tr: "100의 법칙"에 따르면, 어떤 표현이 더 매력적으로 보일 가능성이 높을까요?

segments.src: - (c) They will feel exactly the same
segments.tr: - (c) 두 표현은 정확히 같게 느껴진다

segments.src: ## 📚 Key Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 핵심 용어

segments.src: - **Reference price:** The benchmark a shopper uses to decide whether a price is high, low, or fair.
segments.tr: - **기준 가격:** 소비자가 가격이 비싼지, 싼지, 또는 적정한지 판단할 때 사용하는 기준점입니다.

segments.src: - **Internal reference price:** A benchmark stored in memory, based on past purchases, expectations, or what feels "normal."
segments.tr: - **내부 기준 가격:** 과거 구매, 기대치, 또는 "보통"이라고 느끼는 가격에 기반해 기억 속에 저장된 기준점입니다.

segments.src: - **External reference price:** A benchmark supplied at the point of sale, such as a "Was" price, MSRP, or a nearby comparison product.
segments.tr: - **외부 기준 가격:** "Was" 가격, MSRP, 또는 인근의 비교 제품처럼 판매 시점에 제공되는 기준점입니다.

segments.src: - **Left-digit effect:** The tendency to focus on a price's first digit, so $2.99 feels noticeably cheaper than $3.00.
segments.tr: - **왼쪽 자릿수 효과:** 가격의 첫 자릿수에 집중하는 경향으로, 그래서 $2.99가 $3.00보다 눈에 띄게 싸게 느껴집니다.

segments.src: - **Anchoring:** The tendency for an initial number to pull later judgments toward it.
segments.tr: - **앵커링:** 처음 제시된 숫자가 이후의 판단을 그 숫자 쪽으로 끌어당기는 경향입니다.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 (b).
segments.tr: *정답: Q1 (b).

segments.src: The seller is supplying the comparison point, so it's an external reference price; an internal one would come from your own memory.
segments.tr: 판매자가 비교 기준을 제공하므로 외부 기준 가격입니다. 내부 기준 가격은 자신의 기억에서 나옵니다.

segments.src: Q2 O.
segments.tr: Q2 O.

segments.src: Going from $4.00 to $3.99 changes the leftmost digit (4 → 3), which is where the effect is strongest; $4.50 to $4.49 keeps the leftmost digit the same.
segments.tr: $4.00에서 $3.99로 바뀌면 가장 왼쪽 자릿수(4→3)가 바뀌며, 이때 효과가 가장 강합니다. $4.50에서 $4.49로 바뀌면 가장 왼쪽 자릿수가 같습니다.

segments.src: For items above roughly $100, the dollar amount ($180) is usually a bigger, more impressive-looking number than the percentage (15%), even though they describe the same discount.*
segments.tr: 약 $100을 넘는 상품의 경우, 두 표현이 같은 할인을 설명하더라도 금액($180)이 퍼센트(15%)보다 보통 더 크고 인상적으로 보이는 숫자입니다.*

zh.title: [消费心理学 #11] 为什么 $19.99 感觉比 $20 便宜：价格的心理学

segments.src: > A price is never judged alone. We compare it to a number in our heads, read it from left to right, and react to how a discount is framed, so the same dollar amount can feel like a bargain or a rip-off.
segments.tr: > 价格从来不是孤立被评判的。我们会把它与脑海中的一个数字做比较，从左往右读，并对折扣的呈现方式作出反应，因此同样的金额可能让人觉得是捡到便宜，也可能觉得被宰了。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Economics textbooks often treat price as a simple fact: a product costs $20, and you decide whether it is worth $20 to you.
segments.tr: 经济学教科书通常把价格当作一个简单的事实：一件商品值 20 美元，而你决定它对你来说是否值 20 美元。

segments.src: Real shoppers don't work that way.
segments.tr: 真实的消费者并不是这样运作的。

segments.src: Consumer psychology shows that people judge prices **relative to something else**, and that small details in how a price is shown can change how it feels.
segments.tr: 消费心理学表明，人们是**相对于其他东西**来判断价格的，而价格呈现方式中的一些细节会改变它给人的感受。

segments.src: Three ideas explain most of this.
segments.tr: 有三个概念可以解释其中的大部分现象。

segments.src: Reference price: "Compared to what?"**
segments.tr: 参考价格：“与什么相比？”**

segments.src: A reference price is the benchmark you use to decide whether a price is high or low.
segments.tr: 参考价格是你用来判断某个价格高还是低的基准。

segments.src: It comes from two places:
segments.tr: 它来自两个方面：

segments.src: - **Internal reference price** is the number already in your memory: what you paid last time, what you think is "normal," what a friend said they paid.
segments.tr: - **内部参考价格**是已经存在于你记忆中的数字：你上次花了多少钱、你认为“正常”的价格是多少、朋友说他们花了多少钱。

segments.src: - **External reference price** is a number the seller shows you: a "Was $80" tag, a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP), or a pricier item placed right next to the one being sold.
segments.tr: - **外部参考价格**是卖家展示给你的数字：“原价 80 美元”的标签、厂商建议零售价（MSRP），或者紧挨着待售商品摆放的一件更贵的商品。

segments.src: A $60 jacket feels like a deal if you expected $90, and feels expensive if you expected $40.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9: the left-digit effect**
segments.tr: 以 9 结尾的价格：左位数效应**

segments.src: Why do so many prices end in .99 or 9?
segments.tr: 为什么这么多价格以 .99 或 9 结尾？

segments.src: One well-supported explanation is the **left-digit effect**.
segments.tr: 一个得到较多支持的解释是**左位数效应**。

segments.src: We read numbers left to right, and the first digit gets more attention than the rest.
segments.tr: 我们从左往右读数字，最左边的数位比其他数位获得更多注意。

segments.src: So $19.99 tends to register as "nineteen-something," not "basically twenty," even though the difference is a single cent.
segments.tr: 因此，$19.99 往往会被理解为“十几块多”，而不是“基本就是二十”，尽管两者只相差一分钱。

segments.src: Prices ending in 9 also carry a second signal: many shoppers have learned to associate them with sales and discounts.

segments.src: That said, 9-endings are not magic.

segments.src: Luxury and premium brands often prefer round numbers ($200, not $199.99) precisely because round prices signal quality rather than bargain.
segments.tr: 奢侈品和高端品牌往往偏好整数价格（比如 200 美元，而不是 199.99 美元），正是因为整数价格传递的是品质，而不是划算。

segments.src: Discount perception: framing the savings**
segments.tr: 折扣感知：如何呈现节省的金额**

segments.src: The same discount can be described in different ways, and the description matters.
segments.tr: 同样的折扣可以用不同的方式描述，而描述方式很重要。

segments.src: - **Percent vs. dollars:** For cheaper items, a percentage often looks bigger ("25% off" a $12 item sounds better than "$3 off"). For expensive items, the dollar figure often looks bigger ("$300 off" a $1,500 laptop sounds better than "20% off"). Marketers sometimes call this the "rule of 100": below $100, show the percent; above $100, show the dollars. It's a useful rule of thumb, not a law.
segments.tr: - **百分比与金额：** 对于便宜的商品，百分比往往看起来更大（一件 12 美元的商品标注“减价 25%”，听起来比“减 3 美元”更吸引人）。对于昂贵的商品，金额往往看起来更大（一台 1,500 美元的笔记本标注“减 300 美元”，听起来比“减价 20%”更吸引人）。营销人员有时把这称为“100 法则”：低于 100 美元时展示百分比，高于 100 美元时展示金额。这是一个有用的经验法则，而不是定律。

segments.src: - **Relative savings:** People will drive across town to save $10 on a $30 item but often won't for $10 off a $1,000 item, even though the savings are identical. We tend to judge savings as a proportion of the price, not in absolute dollars.
segments.tr: - **相对节省：** 人们愿意开车穿过大半个城市去省下 30 美元商品上的 10 美元，却往往不会为了省下 1,000 美元商品上的 10 美元这样做，尽管节省的金额完全相同。我们倾向于按占价格的比例来判断节省的金额，而不是看绝对金额。

segments.src: In 2012, **JCPenney** tried to simplify its pricing.
segments.tr: 2012 年，**JCPenney**（杰西潘尼）试图简化其定价。

segments.src: Instead of marking items up and then running constant sales and coupons, it moved to "fair and square" everyday prices that were often similar to what shoppers had been paying after discounts anyway.
segments.tr: 它没有先提高标价、再频繁搞促销和优惠券，而是改为推行“公平实在”的日常定价，这些价格通常与顾客打折后一直支付的价格相差无几。

segments.src: On paper, customers weren't losing money.
segments.tr: 从账面上看，顾客并没有多花钱。

segments.src: But they lost the "Was $50, now $29.99" comparison, and with it the feeling of winning a deal.
segments.tr: 但他们失去了“原价 50 美元，现价 29.99 美元”这种对比，也失去了随之而来的“占到便宜”的感觉。

segments.src: Sales fell sharply, the CEO behind the change was replaced in 2013, and the company brought back its sales and coupons.
segments.tr: 销量急剧下滑，推动这一改革的首席执行官于 2013 年被替换，公司也重新恢复了促销和优惠券。

segments.src: You can see the same psychology on any weekend at Target, Walmart, or on Amazon: a crossed-out "List Price," a "Save 30%" badge, or a $29.99 tag sitting next to a $49.99 "premium" version.
segments.tr: 你在任何一个周末的 Target、Walmart 或 Amazon 上都能看到同样的心理机制：被划掉的“List Price（标价）”、“节省 30%”的标签，或者一件 49.99 美元的“高端”版本旁边摆着一个 29.99 美元的标签。

segments.src: Each one is designed to give you a reference point that makes the price in front of you look reasonable.
segments.tr: 每一种设计都是为了给你一个参考点，让你眼前的价格看起来很合理。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. We judge prices against a **reference price**, either remembered (internal) or shown by the seller (external), so context can make the same price feel cheap or expensive.
segments.tr: 1. 我们会用**参考价格**来衡量价格，它要么来自记忆（内部），要么由卖家展示（外部），因此语境可以让同一个价格显得便宜或昂贵。

segments.src: 2. Prices ending in 9 work partly because of the **left-digit effect** and partly because shoppers link them with sales; round prices tend to signal quality instead.
segments.tr: 2. 以 9 结尾的价格，一部分靠的是**左位数效应**，另一部分是因为购物者把它们与促销联系在一起；相反，整数价格更倾向于传递品质。

segments.src: 3. How a **discount** is framed (percent vs. dollars, relative vs. absolute savings) changes how big it feels, even when the money saved is the same.
segments.tr: 3. **折扣**的呈现方式（百分比还是金额、相对节省还是绝对节省）会改变它给人的感觉大小，即使节省的钱完全相同。

segments.src: ## 📚 Key Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 关键术语

es.title: [Psicología del consumidor #11] Por qué $19.99 parece más barato que $20: la psicología del precio

segments.src: > A price is never judged alone. We compare it to a number in our heads, read it from left to right, and react to how a discount is framed, so the same dollar amount can feel like a bargain or a rip-off.
segments.tr: > Un precio nunca se juzga por sí solo. Lo comparamos con una cifra que tenemos en la cabeza, lo leemos de izquierda a derecha y reaccionamos a la forma en que se presenta un descuento, de modo que la misma cantidad de dinero puede parecer una ganga o un abuso.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Economics textbooks often treat price as a simple fact: a product costs $20, and you decide whether it is worth $20 to you.
segments.tr: Los libros de economía suelen tratar el precio como un hecho simple: un producto cuesta $20 y tú decides si vale $20 para ti.

segments.src: Real shoppers don't work that way.
segments.tr: Los compradores reales no funcionan así.

segments.src: Consumer psychology shows that people judge prices **relative to something else**, and that small details in how a price is shown can change how it feels.
segments.tr: La psicología del consumidor muestra que las personas juzgan los precios **en relación con algo más**, y que pequeños detalles en la forma de mostrar un precio pueden cambiar cómo se siente.

segments.src: Three ideas explain most of this.
segments.tr: Tres ideas explican gran parte de esto.

segments.src: Reference price: "Compared to what?"**
segments.tr: Precio de referencia: «¿comparado con qué?»**

segments.src: A reference price is the benchmark you use to decide whether a price is high or low.
segments.tr: Un precio de referencia es el punto de comparación que usas para decidir si un precio es alto o bajo.

segments.src: It comes from two places:
segments.tr: Procede de dos fuentes:

segments.src: - **Internal reference price** is the number already in your memory: what you paid last time, what you think is "normal," what a friend said they paid.
segments.tr: - **El precio de referencia interno** es la cifra que ya tienes en la memoria: lo que pagaste la última vez, lo que consideras «normal» o lo que un amigo te dijo que pagó.

segments.src: - **External reference price** is a number the seller shows you: a "Was $80" tag, a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP), or a pricier item placed right next to the one being sold.
segments.tr: - **El precio de referencia externo** es una cifra que te muestra el vendedor: una etiqueta de «Antes $80», el precio de venta sugerido por el fabricante (MSRP) o un artículo más caro colocado justo al lado del que se vende.

segments.src: A $60 jacket feels like a deal if you expected $90, and feels expensive if you expected $40.
segments.tr: Una chaqueta de $60 parece una oferta si esperabas pagar $90, y parece cara si esperabas pagar $40.

segments.src: The price itself didn't change.
segments.tr: El precio en sí no cambió.

segments.src: The comparison did.
segments.tr: Cambió la comparación.

segments.src: This connects to *anchoring*, the tendency for the first number we see to pull later judgments toward it.
segments.tr: Esto se relaciona con el *anclaje*, la tendencia de la primera cifra que vemos a arrastrar hacia ella los juicios posteriores.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9: the left-digit effect**
segments.tr: Precios que terminan en 9: el efecto del dígito izquierdo**

segments.src: Why do so many prices end in .99 or 9?
segments.tr: ¿Por qué tantos precios terminan en ,99 o en 9?

segments.src: One well-supported explanation is the **left-digit effect**.
segments.tr: Una explicación bien respaldada es el **efecto del dígito izquierdo**.

segments.src: We read numbers left to right, and the first digit gets more attention than the rest.
segments.tr: Leemos los números de izquierda a derecha, y el primer dígito recibe más atención que los demás.

segments.src: So $19.99 tends to register as "nineteen-something," not "basically twenty," even though the difference is a single cent.
segments.tr: Así, $19.99 tiende a registrarse como «diecinueve y algo», y no como «prácticamente veinte», aunque la diferencia sea de un solo centavo.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9 also carry a second signal: many shoppers have learned to associate them with sales and discounts.
segments.tr: Los precios que terminan en 9 también transmiten una segunda señal: muchos compradores han aprendido a asociarlos con rebajas y descuentos.

segments.src: In one well-known field experiment with a women's clothing catalog, the same dress sold more at $39 than at either $34 or $44.
segments.tr: En un experimento de campo muy conocido con un catálogo de ropa de mujer, el mismo vestido se vendió más a $39 que a $34 o a $44.

segments.src: That said, 9-endings are not magic.

segments.src: Luxury and premium brands often prefer round numbers ($200, not $199.99) precisely because round prices signal quality rather than bargain.
segments.tr: Las marcas de lujo y premium suelen preferir cifras redondas ($200, no $199.99) precisamente porque los precios redondos transmiten calidad en lugar de ganga.

segments.src: Discount perception: framing the savings**
segments.tr: Percepción del descuento: cómo se presenta el ahorro**

segments.src: The same discount can be described in different ways, and the description matters.
segments.tr: El mismo descuento puede describirse de distintas maneras, y la descripción importa.

segments.src: - **Percent vs. dollars:** For cheaper items, a percentage often looks bigger ("25% off" a $12 item sounds better than "$3 off"). For expensive items, the dollar figure often looks bigger ("$300 off" a $1,500 laptop sounds better than "20% off"). Marketers sometimes call this the "rule of 100": below $100, show the percent; above $100, show the dollars. It's a useful rule of thumb, not a law.
segments.tr: - **Porcentaje frente a dólares:** En artículos baratos, un porcentaje suele parecer más grande («25 % de descuento» en un artículo de $12 suena mejor que «$3 de descuento»). En artículos caros, la cifra en dólares suele parecer más grande («$300 de descuento» en una laptop de $1,500 suena mejor que «20 % de descuento»). Los mercadólogos a veces llaman a esto la «regla del 100»: por debajo de $100, muestra el porcentaje; por encima de $100, muestra los dólares. Es una guía práctica útil, no una ley.

segments.src: - **Relative savings:** People will drive across town to save $10 on a $30 item but often won't for $10 off a $1,000 item, even though the savings are identical. We tend to judge savings as a proportion of the price, not in absolute dollars.
segments.tr: - **Ahorro relativo:** Las personas cruzarán la ciudad para ahorrar $10 en un artículo de $30, pero a menudo no lo harán por $10 de descuento en un artículo de $1,000, aunque el ahorro sea idéntico. Tendemos a juzgar el ahorro como una proporción del precio, no en dólares absolutos.

segments.src: > A price is never judged alone. We compare it to a number in our heads, read it from left to right, and react to how a discount is framed, so the same dollar amount can feel like a bargain or a rip-off.
segments.tr: > لا يُحكم على السعر أبداً بمعزل عن غيره. نقارنه برقم في أذهاننا، ونقرؤه من اليسار إلى اليمين، ونتفاعل مع طريقة عرض الخصم، فيبدو المبلغ نفسه صفقة رابحة أو عملية سلب.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## فكرة اليوم

segments.src: Economics textbooks often treat price as a simple fact: a product costs $20, and you decide whether it is worth $20 to you.
segments.tr: تتعامل كتب الاقتصاد عادةً مع السعر كحقيقة بسيطة: المنتج يكلّف 20 دولاراً، وأنت تقرر ما إذا كان يستحق 20 دولاراً بالنسبة إليك.

segments.src: Real shoppers don't work that way.
segments.tr: لكن المتسوقين الحقيقيين لا يفكرون بهذه الطريقة.

segments.src: Consumer psychology shows that people judge prices **relative to something else**, and that small details in how a price is shown can change how it feels.
segments.tr: تُظهر علوم سلوك المستهلك أن الناس يحكمون على الأسعار **بالنسبة إلى شيء آخر**، وأن تفاصيل صغيرة في طريقة عرض السعر قد تغيّر الإحساس به.

segments.src: Three ideas explain most of this.
segments.tr: تفسّر ثلاث أفكار معظم ذلك.

segments.src: Reference price: "Compared to what?"**
segments.tr: السعر المرجعي: "مقارنةً بماذا؟"**

segments.src: A reference price is the benchmark you use to decide whether a price is high or low.
segments.tr: السعر المرجعي هو المعيار الذي تستخدمه لتحديد ما إذا كان السعر مرتفعاً أو منخفضاً.

segments.src: It comes from two places:
segments.tr: ويأتي من مصدرين:

segments.src: - **Internal reference price** is the number already in your memory: what you paid last time, what you think is "normal," what a friend said they paid.
segments.tr: - **السعر المرجعي الداخلي** هو الرقم المحفوظ في ذاكرتك بالفعل: ما دفعته في المرة السابقة، وما تعتبره "طبيعياً"، وما قاله صديق أنه دفعه.

segments.src: - **External reference price** is a number the seller shows you: a "Was $80" tag, a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP), or a pricier item placed right next to the one being sold.
segments.tr: - **السعر المرجعي الخارجي** هو رقم يعرضه البائع عليك: وسم "كان السعر 80 دولاراً"، أو السعر المقترح للبيع بالتجزئة من الشركة المصنِّعة (MSRP)، أو منتج أغلى يوضع بجانب المنتج المعروض للبيع.

segments.src: A $60 jacket feels like a deal if you expected $90, and feels expensive if you expected $40.
segments.tr: تبدو سترة بسعر 60 دولاراً صفقة إذا كنت تتوقع 90 دولاراً، وتبدو باهظة إذا كنت تتوقع 40 دولاراً.

segments.src: The price itself didn't change.
segments.tr: السعر نفسه لم يتغير.

segments.src: The comparison did.
segments.tr: المقارنة هي التي تغيّرت.

segments.src: This connects to *anchoring*, the tendency for the first number we see to pull later judgments toward it.
segments.tr: ويرتبط هذا بـ*الترسيخ* (Anchoring)، أي ميل الرقم الأول الذي نراه إلى جذب أحكامنا اللاحقة نحوه.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9: the left-digit effect**
segments.tr: الأسعار المنتهية بالرقم 9: تأثير الرقم الأيسر**

segments.src: Why do so many prices end in .99 or 9?
segments.tr: لماذا تنتهي كثير من الأسعار بـ .99 أو 9؟

segments.src: One well-supported explanation is the **left-digit effect**.
segments.tr: أحد التفسيرات المدعومة جيداً هو **تأثير الرقم الأيسر**.

segments.src: We read numbers left to right, and the first digit gets more attention than the rest.
segments.tr: نقرأ الأرقام من اليسار إلى اليمين، ويحظى الرقم الأول بانتباه أكبر من بقية الأرقام.

segments.src: So $19.99 tends to register as "nineteen-something," not "basically twenty," even though the difference is a single cent.
segments.tr: لذلك يُسجَّل 19.99 دولاراً غالباً على أنه "تسعة عشر وشيء"، لا "عشرون تقريباً"، مع أن الفرق سنت واحد فقط.

segments.src: Research has found the effect is strongest when the leftmost digit changes ($2.99 vs.
segments.tr: وقد وجدت الأبحاث أن التأثير يكون أقوى عندما يتغير الرقم الأيسر (2.99 دولاراً مقابل

segments.src: $3.00), not when it stays the same ($2.89 vs.
segments.tr: 3.00 دولار)، لا عندما يبقى كما هو (2.89 دولاراً مقابل
2.90 دولار).

segments.src: Prices ending in 9 also carry a second signal: many shoppers have learned to associate them with sales and discounts.
segments.tr: وتحمل الأسعار المنتهية بالرقم 9 إشارة ثانية: فقد تعلّم كثير من المتسوقين ربطها بالتخفيضات والعروض.

segments.src: In one well-known field experiment with a women's clothing catalog, the same dress sold more at $39 than at either $34 or $44.
segments.tr: وفي تجربة ميدانية معروفة مع كتالوج لملابس النساء، بيع الفستان نفسه أكثر عند 39 دولاراً منه عند 34 دولاراً أو 44 دولاراً.

segments.src: The 9-ending outsold even a *lower* price.
segments.tr: فقد تفوّق السعر المنتهي بالرقم 9 حتى على سعر *أقل*.

segments.src: That said, 9-endings are not magic.
segments.tr: ومع ذلك، الأسعار المنتهية بالرقم 9 ليست سحراً.

segments.src: Luxury and premium brands often prefer round numbers ($200, not $199.99) precisely because round prices signal quality rather than bargain.
segments.tr: فالعلامات التجارية الفاخرة والراقية تفضّل غالباً الأرقام المستديرة (200 دولار، لا 199.99 دولاراً) تحديداً لأن الأسعار المستديرة تدل على الجودة لا على الصفقة.

segments.src: Discount perception: framing the savings**
segments.tr: إدراك الخصم: طريقة تأطير التوفير**

segments.src: The same discount can be described in different ways, and the description matters.
segments.tr: يمكن وصف الخصم نفسه بطرق مختلفة، ويهم الوصف.

segments.src: - **Percent vs. dollars:** For cheaper items, a percentage often looks bigger ("25% off" a $12 item sounds better than "$3 off"). For expensive items, the dollar figure often looks bigger ("$300 off" a $1,500 laptop sounds better than "20% off"). Marketers sometimes call this the "rule of 100": below $100, show the percent; above $100, show the dollars. It's a useful rule of thumb, not a law.
segments.tr: - **النسبة المئوية مقابل الدولارات:** بالنسبة إلى المنتجات الرخيصة، غالباً ما تبدو النسبة المئوية أكبر ("خصم 25%" على منتج بسعر 12 دولاراً يبدو أفضل من "خصم 3 دولارات"). وبالنسبة إلى المنتجات الغالية، غالباً ما يبدو الرقم بالدولار أكبر ("خصم 300 دولار" على حاسوب محمول بسعر 1,500 دولار يبدو أفضل من "خصم 20%"). ويسمي المسوّقون أحياناً هذا "قاعدة 100": دون 100 دولار، اعرض النسبة المئوية؛ وفوق 100 دولار، اعرض المبلغ بالدولار. إنها قاعدة إبهام مفيدة، لا قانون.

segments.src: - **Relative savings:** People will drive across town to save $10 on a $30 item but often won't for $10 off a $1,000 item, even though the savings are identical. We tend to judge savings as a proportion of the price, not in absolute dollars.
segments.tr: - **التوفير النسبي:** يقطع الناس مسافة عبر المدينة لتوفير 10 دولارات على منتج بسعر 30 دولاراً، لكنهم كثيراً ما لا يفعلون ذلك مع خصم 10 دولارات على منتج بسعر 1,000 دولار، مع أن مبلغ التوفير واحد. نميل إلى تقدير التوفير كنسبة من السعر، لا بالدولارات المطلقة.

segments.src: We read numbers left to right, and the first digit gets more attention than the rest.
segments.tr: Nous lisons les nombres de gauche à droite, et le premier chiffre retient davantage notre attention que les autres.

segments.src: Discount perception: framing the savings**
segments.tr: Perception de la remise : la façon de présenter l'économie**

segments.src: The same discount can be described in different ways, and the description matters.
segments.tr: Une même remise peut être décrite de différentes manières, et la description compte.

segments.src: - **Percent vs. dollars:** For cheaper items, a percentage often looks bigger ("25% off" a $12 item sounds better than "$3 off"). For expensive items, the dollar figure often looks bigger ("$300 off" a $1,500 laptop sounds better than "20% off"). Marketers sometimes call this the "rule of 100": below $100, show the percent; above $100, show the dollars. It's a useful rule of thumb, not a law.
segments.tr: - **Pourcentage ou montant en dollars :** Pour les articles bon marché, un pourcentage paraît souvent plus important (« 25 % de réduction » sur un article à 12 $ sonne mieux que « 3 $ de réduction »). Pour les articles chers, le montant en dollars paraît souvent plus important (« 300 $ de réduction » sur un ordinateur portable à 1 500 $ sonne mieux que « 20 % de réduction »). Les spécialistes du marketing appellent parfois cela la « règle des 100 » : en dessous de 100 $, on affiche le pourcentage ; au-dessus de 100 $, on affiche le montant. C'est une règle empirique utile, et non une loi.

segments.src: - **Relative savings:** People will drive across town to save $10 on a $30 item but often won't for $10 off a $1,000 item, even though the savings are identical. We tend to judge savings as a proportion of the price, not in absolute dollars.
segments.tr: - **Économie relative :** Les gens feront le tour de la ville pour économiser 10 $ sur un article à 30 $, mais souvent pas pour 10 $ de réduction sur un article à 1 000 $, alors que l'économie est identique. Nous avons tendance à évaluer une économie en proportion du prix, et non en valeur absolue en dollars.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept

segments.src: Economics textbooks often treat price as a simple fact: a product costs $20, and you decide whether it is worth $20 to you.

segments.src: Real shoppers don't work that way.
segments.tr: Consumidores reais não funcionam assim.

segments.src: Consumer psychology shows that people judge prices **relative to something else**, and that small details in how a price is shown can change how it feels.
segments.tr: A psicologia do consumidor mostra que as pessoas julgam os preços **em relação a outra coisa**, e que pequenos detalhes na forma como um preço é exibido podem mudar a sensação que ele provoca.

in.title: [Psikologi Konsumen #11] Mengapa $19.99 Terasa Lebih Murah daripada $20: Psikologi Harga

segments.src: > A price is never judged alone. We compare it to a number in our heads, read it from left to right, and react to how a discount is framed, so the same dollar amount can feel like a bargain or a rip-off.
segments.tr: > Harga tidak pernah dinilai sendirian. Kita membandingkannya dengan angka di kepala, membacanya dari kiri ke kanan, dan bereaksi terhadap cara diskon disajikan, sehingga nominal yang sama bisa terasa seperti penawaran bagus atau pemerasan.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Economics textbooks often treat price as a simple fact: a product costs $20, and you decide whether it is worth $20 to you.
segments.tr: Buku teks ekonomi sering memperlakukan harga sebagai fakta sederhana: sebuah produk berharga $20, dan Anda memutuskan apakah produk itu layak $20 bagi Anda.

segments.src: Real shoppers don't work that way.
segments.tr: Pembeli sungguhan tidak bekerja seperti itu.

segments.src: Consumer psychology shows that people judge prices **relative to something else**, and that small details in how a price is shown can change how it feels.
segments.tr: Psikologi konsumen menunjukkan bahwa orang menilai harga **secara relatif terhadap sesuatu yang lain**, dan detail kecil dalam cara harga ditampilkan dapat mengubah bagaimana harga itu terasa.

segments.src: Three ideas explain most of this.
segments.tr: Tiga gagasan menjelaskan sebagian besar hal ini.

segments.src: Reference price: "Compared to what?"**
segments.tr: Harga acuan: "Dibandingkan dengan apa?"**

segments.src: A reference price is the benchmark you use to decide whether a price is high or low.
segments.tr: Harga acuan adalah patokan yang Anda gunakan untuk memutuskan apakah suatu harga tinggi atau rendah.

segments.src: It comes from two places:
segments.tr: Patokan ini berasal dari dua sumber:

segments.src: - **Internal reference price** is the number already in your memory: what you paid last time, what you think is "normal," what a friend said they paid.
segments.tr: - **Harga acuan internal** adalah angka yang sudah ada dalam ingatan Anda: harga yang Anda bayar terakhir kali, yang Anda anggap "normal", atau yang dikatakan teman Anda sebagai harganya.

segments.src: - **External reference price** is a number the seller shows you: a "Was $80" tag, a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP), or a pricier item placed right next to the one being sold.
segments.tr: - **Harga acuan eksternal** adalah angka yang ditunjukkan penjual kepada Anda: label "Dulu $80", harga eceran yang disarankan produsen (MSRP), atau produk yang lebih mahal yang diletakkan tepat di sebelah produk yang dijual.

segments.src: A $60 jacket feels like a deal if you expected $90, and feels expensive if you expected $40.
segments.tr: Jaket $60 terasa seperti penawaran bagus jika Anda mengira harganya $90, dan terasa mahal jika Anda mengira harganya $40.

segments.src: The price itself didn't change.
segments.tr: Harga itu sendiri tidak berubah.

segments.src: The comparison did.
segments.tr: Yang berubah adalah perbandingannya.

segments.src: This connects to *anchoring*, the tendency for the first number we see to pull later judgments toward it.
segments.tr: Ini terkait dengan *anchoring* (penjangkaran), yaitu kecenderungan angka pertama yang kita lihat untuk menarik penilaian berikutnya ke arahnya.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9: the left-digit effect**
segments.tr: Harga yang berakhiran 9: efek digit kiri**

segments.src: Why do so many prices end in .99 or 9?
segments.tr: Mengapa begitu banyak harga berakhiran .99 atau 9?

segments.src: One well-supported explanation is the **left-digit effect**.
segments.tr: Salah satu penjelasan yang didukung dengan baik adalah **efek digit kiri**.

segments.src: We read numbers left to right, and the first digit gets more attention than the rest.
segments.tr: Kita membaca angka dari kiri ke kanan, dan digit pertama mendapat perhatian lebih besar daripada digit lainnya.

segments.src: So $19.99 tends to register as "nineteen-something," not "basically twenty," even though the difference is a single cent.
segments.tr: Jadi $19.99 cenderung terdaftar sebagai "sembilan belasan", bukan "hampir dua puluh", meskipun selisihnya hanya satu sen.

segments.src: Research has found the effect is strongest when the leftmost digit changes ($2.99 vs.
segments.tr: Penelitian menemukan bahwa efek ini paling kuat ketika digit paling kiri berubah ($2.99 vs.

segments.src: $3.00), not when it stays the same ($2.89 vs.
segments.tr: $3.00), bukan ketika tetap sama ($2.89 vs.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9 also carry a second signal: many shoppers have learned to associate them with sales and discounts.
segments.tr: Harga yang berakhiran 9 juga membawa sinyal kedua: banyak pembeli telah belajar mengaitkannya dengan obral dan diskon.

segments.src: In one well-known field experiment with a women's clothing catalog, the same dress sold more at $39 than at either $34 or $44.
segments.tr: Dalam satu eksperimen lapangan yang terkenal dengan katalog pakaian wanita, gaun yang sama terjual lebih banyak pada $39 dibanding pada $34 maupun $44.

segments.src: The 9-ending outsold even a *lower* price.
segments.tr: Harga berakhiran 9 mengungguli bahkan harga yang *lebih rendah*.

segments.src: That said, 9-endings are not magic.
segments.tr: Meski begitu, harga berakhiran 9 bukanlah hal ajaib.

segments.src: Luxury and premium brands often prefer round numbers ($200, not $199.99) precisely because round prices signal quality rather than bargain.
segments.tr: Merek mewah dan premium sering lebih suka angka bulat ($200, bukan $199.99) justru karena harga bulat menandakan kualitas, bukan penawaran murah.

segments.src: Discount perception: framing the savings**
segments.tr: Persepsi diskon: membingkai penghematan

segments.src: The same discount can be described in different ways, and the description matters.
segments.tr: Diskon yang sama bisa dijelaskan dengan cara yang berbeda, dan cara penjelasannya itu penting.

segments.src: - **Percent vs. dollars:** For cheaper items, a percentage often looks bigger ("25% off" a $12 item sounds better than "$3 off"). For expensive items, the dollar figure often looks bigger ("$300 off" a $1,500 laptop sounds better than "20% off"). Marketers sometimes call this the "rule of 100": below $100, show the percent; above $100, show the dollars. It's a useful rule of thumb, not a law.
segments.tr: - **Persen vs. nominal:** Untuk barang yang lebih murah, persentase sering terlihat lebih besar ("diskon 25%" untuk barang $12 terdengar lebih menarik daripada "diskon $3"). Untuk barang yang mahal, angka nominal sering terlihat lebih besar ("diskon $300" untuk laptop $1,500 terdengar lebih menarik daripada "diskon 20%"). Pemasar kadang menyebut ini "aturan 100": di bawah $100, tampilkan persen; di atas $100, tampilkan nominal. Ini adalah aturan praktis yang berguna, bukan hukum.

segments.src: - **Relative savings:** People will drive across town to save $10 on a $30 item but often won't for $10 off a $1,000 item, even though the savings are identical. We tend to judge savings as a proportion of the price, not in absolute dollars.
segments.tr: - **Penghematan relatif:** Orang akan berkendara lintas kota untuk menghemat $10 pada barang $30, tetapi sering tidak mau melakukannya untuk diskon $10 pada barang $1,000, padahal penghematannya sama persis. Kita cenderung menilai penghematan sebagai proporsi dari harga, bukan dalam nilai nominal mutlak.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: A famous U.S.
segments.tr: Sebuah kisah ritel terkenal di Amerika Serikat

segments.src: retail story shows how strong reference prices are.
segments.tr: menunjukkan betapa kuatnya harga acuan.

segments.src: In 2012, **JCPenney** tried to simplify its pricing.
segments.tr: Pada 2012, **JCPenney** berusaha menyederhanakan penetapan harganya.

segments.src: Instead of marking items up and then running constant sales and coupons, it moved to "fair and square" everyday prices that were often similar to what shoppers had been paying after discounts anyway.
segments.tr: Alih-alih menaikkan harga lalu terus-menerus menjalankan obral dan kupon, perusahaan beralih ke harga harian "adil dan jujur" yang sering kali mirip dengan harga yang sudah dibayar pembeli setelah diskon.

segments.src: On paper, customers weren't losing money.
segments.tr: Di atas kertas, pelanggan tidak kehilangan uang.

segments.src: But they lost the "Was $50, now $29.99" comparison, and with it the feeling of winning a deal.
segments.tr: Namun mereka kehilangan perbandingan "Dulu $50, sekarang $29.99", dan bersamanya perasaan telah mendapatkan penawaran.

segments.src: Sales fell sharply, the CEO behind the change was replaced in 2013, and the company brought back its sales and coupons.
segments.tr: Penjualan anjlok, CEO yang memimpin perubahan itu diganti pada 2013, dan perusahaan kembali menjalankan obral serta kupon.

segments.src: You can see the same psychology on any weekend at Target, Walmart, or on Amazon: a crossed-out "List Price," a "Save 30%" badge, or a $29.99 tag sitting next to a $49.99 "premium" version.
segments.tr: Psikologi yang sama bisa Anda lihat pada akhir pekan mana pun di Target, Walmart, atau Amazon: harga "List Price" yang dicoret, lencana "Hemat 30%", atau label $29.99 yang berdampingan dengan versi "premium" $49.99.

segments.src: Each one is designed to give you a reference point that makes the price in front of you look reasonable.
segments.tr: Masing-masing dirancang untuk memberi Anda titik acuan yang membuat harga di depan mata tampak wajar.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan 3 Baris

segments.src: 1. We judge prices against a **reference price**, either remembered (internal) or shown by the seller (external), so context can make the same price feel cheap or expensive.
segments.tr: 1. Kita menilai harga terhadap **harga acuan**, yang bisa berupa ingatan (internal) atau yang ditampilkan penjual (eksternal), sehingga konteks dapat membuat harga yang sama terasa murah atau mahal.

segments.src: 2. Prices ending in 9 work partly because of the **left-digit effect** and partly because shoppers link them with sales; round prices tend to signal quality instead.
segments.tr: 2. Harga yang berakhiran 9 berhasil sebagian karena **efek digit kiri** dan sebagian karena pembeli mengaitkannya dengan obral; harga bulat justru cenderung menandakan kualitas.

segments.src: 3. How a **discount** is framed (percent vs. dollars, relative vs. absolute savings) changes how big it feels, even when the money saved is the same.
segments.tr: 3. Cara **diskon** dibingkai (persen vs. nominal, penghematan relatif vs. absolut) mengubah seberapa besar kesannya, meskipun uang yang dihemat sama.

segments.src: > A price is never judged alone. We compare it to a number in our heads, read it from left to right, and react to how a discount is framed, so the same dollar amount can feel like a bargain or a rip-off.
segments.tr: > Ein Preis wird nie für sich allein beurteilt. Wir vergleichen ihn mit einer Zahl im Kopf, lesen ihn von links nach rechts und reagieren darauf, wie ein Rabatt dargestellt wird. Deshalb kann dieselbe Summe wie ein Schnäppchen oder wie Abzocke wirken.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Economics textbooks often treat price as a simple fact: a product costs $20, and you decide whether it is worth $20 to you.
segments.tr: Lehrbücher der Volkswirtschaftslehre behandeln den Preis oft als einfache Tatsache: Ein Produkt kostet $20, und du entscheidest, ob es dir $20 wert ist.

segments.src: Real shoppers don't work that way.
segments.tr: Echte Käufer denken aber nicht so.

segments.src: Consumer psychology shows that people judge prices **relative to something else**, and that small details in how a price is shown can change how it feels.
segments.tr: Die Konsumentenpsychologie zeigt, dass Menschen Preise **im Verhältnis zu etwas anderem** beurteilen und dass kleine Details in der Darstellung eines Preises verändern, wie er sich anfühlt.

segments.src: Three ideas explain most of this.
segments.tr: Drei Ideen erklären den größten Teil davon.

segments.src: Reference price: "Compared to what?"**
segments.tr: Referenzpreis: „Verglichen womit?“**

segments.src: A reference price is the benchmark you use to decide whether a price is high or low.
segments.tr: Ein Referenzpreis ist der Maßstab, mit dem du entscheidest, ob ein Preis hoch oder niedrig ist.

segments.src: It comes from two places:
segments.tr: Er stammt aus zwei Quellen:

segments.src: - **Internal reference price** is the number already in your memory: what you paid last time, what you think is "normal," what a friend said they paid.
segments.tr: - **Interner Referenzpreis** ist die Zahl, die bereits in deinem Gedächtnis gespeichert ist: was du das letzte Mal bezahlt hast, was du für „normal“ hältst oder was ein Freund für etwas bezahlt hat.

segments.src: - **External reference price** is a number the seller shows you: a "Was $80" tag, a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP), or a pricier item placed right next to the one being sold.
segments.tr: - **Externer Referenzpreis** ist eine Zahl, die dir der Verkäufer zeigt: ein Schild „Früher $80“, eine unverbindliche Preisempfehlung des Herstellers (UVP) oder ein teureres Produkt direkt neben dem angebotenen.

segments.src: A $60 jacket feels like a deal if you expected $90, and feels expensive if you expected $40.
segments.tr: Eine Jacke für $60 wirkt wie ein Schnäppchen, wenn du $90 erwartet hast, und wie teuer, wenn du $40 erwartet hast.

segments.src: The price itself didn't change.
segments.tr: Der Preis selbst hat sich nicht geändert.

segments.src: The comparison did.
segments.tr: Der Vergleich hat sich geändert.

segments.src: This connects to *anchoring*, the tendency for the first number we see to pull later judgments toward it.
segments.tr: Das hängt mit dem *Ankereffekt* zusammen, also der Tendenz, dass die erste Zahl, die wir sehen, spätere Urteile in ihre Richtung zieht.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9: the left-digit effect**
segments.tr: Preise mit der Endziffer 9: der Linksziffer-Effekt**

segments.src: Why do so many prices end in .99 or 9?
segments.tr: Warum enden so viele Preise auf .99 oder 9?

segments.src: One well-supported explanation is the **left-digit effect**.
segments.tr: Eine gut belegte Erklärung ist der **Linksziffer-Effekt**.

segments.src: We read numbers left to right, and the first digit gets more attention than the rest.
segments.tr: Wir lesen Zahlen von links nach rechts, und die erste Ziffer bekommt mehr Aufmerksamkeit als die übrigen.

segments.src: So $19.99 tends to register as "nineteen-something," not "basically twenty," even though the difference is a single cent.
segments.tr: Deshalb wird $19.99 eher als „neunzehn und etwas“ wahrgenommen und nicht als „praktisch zwanzig“, obwohl der Unterschied nur einen Cent beträgt.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9 also carry a second signal: many shoppers have learned to associate them with sales and discounts.
segments.tr: Preise mit der Endziffer 9 senden außerdem ein zweites Signal: Viele Käufer haben gelernt, sie mit Sonderangeboten und Rabatten zu verbinden.

segments.src: In one well-known field experiment with a women's clothing catalog, the same dress sold more at $39 than at either $34 or $44.
segments.tr: In einem bekannten Feldexperiment mit dem Katalog eines Damenbekleidungsversandhändlers verkaufte sich dasselbe Kleid bei $39 besser als bei $34 oder $44.

segments.src: The 9-ending outsold even a *lower* price.

segments.src: That said, 9-endings are not magic.
segments.tr: Allerdings sind Endziffern auf 9 kein Zaubermittel.

segments.src: Luxury and premium brands often prefer round numbers ($200, not $199.99) precisely because round prices signal quality rather than bargain.
segments.tr: Luxus- und Premiummarken bevorzugen oft runde Preise ($200 statt $199.99), genau weil runde Preise für Qualität stehen und nicht für ein Schnäppchen.

segments.src: Discount perception: framing the savings**
segments.tr: Die Wahrnehmung von Rabatten: wie die Ersparnis dargestellt wird**

segments.src: The same discount can be described in different ways, and the description matters.
segments.tr: Derselbe Rabatt lässt sich auf verschiedene Arten beschreiben, und die Beschreibung macht einen Unterschied.

segments.src: - **Percent vs. dollars:** For cheaper items, a percentage often looks bigger ("25% off" a $12 item sounds better than "$3 off"). For expensive items, the dollar figure often looks bigger ("$300 off" a $1,500 laptop sounds better than "20% off"). Marketers sometimes call this the "rule of 100": below $100, show the percent; above $100, show the dollars. It's a useful rule of thumb, not a law.
segments.tr: - **Prozent vs. Dollarbetrag:** Bei günstigen Artikeln wirkt ein Prozentsatz oft größer („25 % Rabatt“ auf einen $12-Artikel klingt besser als „$3 Rabatt“). Bei teuren Artikeln wirkt oft der Dollarbetrag größer („$300 Rabatt“ auf einen Laptop für $1,500 klingt besser als „20 % Rabatt“). Marketingleute nennen das manchmal die „Regel der 100“: Unter $100 den Prozentsatz zeigen, über $100 den Betrag. Das ist eine brauchbare Faustregel, aber kein Gesetz.

segments.src: - **Relative savings:** People will drive across town to save $10 on a $30 item but often won't for $10 off a $1,000 item, even though the savings are identical. We tend to judge savings as a proportion of the price, not in absolute dollars.
segments.tr: - **Relative Ersparnis:** Menschen fahren quer durch die Stadt, um $10 bei einem $30-Artikel zu sparen, tun das aber oft nicht für $10 Rabatt auf einen $1,000-Artikel, obwohl die Ersparnis identisch ist. Wir beurteilen Ersparnisse eher als Anteil am Preis als in absoluten Beträgen.

segments.src: > A price is never judged alone. We compare it to a number in our heads, read it from left to right, and react to how a discount is framed, so the same dollar amount can feel like a bargain or a rip-off.
segments.tr: > Một mức giá không bao giờ được đánh giá riêng lẻ. Chúng ta so sánh nó với một con số trong đầu, đọc từ trái sang phải, và phản ứng với cách một khoản giảm giá được trình bày, nên cùng một số tiền có thể khiến người ta thấy là món hời hoặc là bị chặt chém.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Economics textbooks often treat price as a simple fact: a product costs $20, and you decide whether it is worth $20 to you.
segments.tr: Sách giáo khoa kinh tế thường coi giá là một sự thật đơn giản: một sản phẩm có giá $20, và bạn quyết định xem nó có đáng $20 đối với bạn hay không.

segments.src: Real shoppers don't work that way.
segments.tr: Người mua thực tế không suy nghĩ như vậy.

segments.src: Consumer psychology shows that people judge prices **relative to something else**, and that small details in how a price is shown can change how it feels.
segments.tr: Tâm lý người tiêu dùng cho thấy mọi người đánh giá giá **so với một thứ khác**, và những chi tiết nhỏ trong cách hiển thị giá có thể thay đổi cảm nhận về nó.

segments.src: Three ideas explain most of this.
segments.tr: Ba ý tưởng sau giải thích phần lớn hiện tượng này.

segments.src: Reference price: "Compared to what?"**
segments.tr: Giá tham chiếu: "So với cái gì?"**

segments.src: A reference price is the benchmark you use to decide whether a price is high or low.
segments.tr: Giá tham chiếu là mốc mà bạn dùng để quyết định một mức giá cao hay thấp.

segments.src: It comes from two places:
segments.tr: Nó đến từ hai nguồn:

segments.src: - **Internal reference price** is the number already in your memory: what you paid last time, what you think is "normal," what a friend said they paid.
segments.tr: - **Giá tham chiếu nội tại** là con số đã có sẵn trong trí nhớ bạn: điều bạn đã trả lần trước, điều bạn cho là "bình thường", điều bạn bè nói họ đã trả.

segments.src: - **External reference price** is a number the seller shows you: a "Was $80" tag, a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP), or a pricier item placed right next to the one being sold.
segments.tr: - **Giá tham chiếu bên ngoài** là con số người bán đưa ra cho bạn: nhãn "Giá cũ $80", giá bán lẻ đề xuất của nhà sản xuất (MSRP), hoặc một sản phẩm đắt hơn đặt ngay cạnh sản phẩm đang bán.

segments.src: A $60 jacket feels like a deal if you expected $90, and feels expensive if you expected $40.
segments.tr: Một chiếc áo khoác $60 có vẻ là món hời nếu bạn đã kỳ vọng $90, và có vẻ đắt nếu bạn kỳ vọng $40.

segments.src: The price itself didn't change.
segments.tr: Giá không thay đổi.

segments.src: The comparison did.
segments.tr: Thứ thay đổi là phép so sánh.

segments.src: This connects to *anchoring*, the tendency for the first number we see to pull later judgments toward it.
segments.tr: Điều này liên quan đến *neo giá* (anchoring), tức xu hướng con số đầu tiên chúng ta thấy kéo các đánh giá sau đó về phía nó.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9: the left-digit effect**
segments.tr: Giá kết thúc bằng 9: hiệu ứng chữ số đầu**

segments.src: Why do so many prices end in .99 or 9?
segments.tr: Vì sao rất nhiều giá kết thúc bằng .99 hoặc 9?

segments.src: One well-supported explanation is the **left-digit effect**.
segments.tr: Một giải thích được nhiều nghiên cứu ủng hộ là **hiệu ứng chữ số đầu** (left-digit effect).

segments.src: We read numbers left to right, and the first digit gets more attention than the rest.
segments.tr: Chúng ta đọc số từ trái sang phải, và chữ số đầu nhận được nhiều sự chú ý hơn các chữ số còn lại.

segments.src: So $19.99 tends to register as "nineteen-something," not "basically twenty," even though the difference is a single cent.
segments.tr: Vì vậy $19.99 thường được hiểu là "mười chín-và-gì-đó", chứ không phải "gần như hai mươi", dù chênh lệch chỉ là một xu.

segments.src: Prices ending in 9 also carry a second signal: many shoppers have learned to associate them with sales and discounts.
segments.tr: Giá kết thúc bằng 9 còn mang một tín hiệu thứ hai: nhiều người mua đã học cách liên tưởng chúng với đợt giảm giá và khuyến mãi.

segments.src: In one well-known field experiment with a women's clothing catalog, the same dress sold more at $39 than at either $34 or $44.
segments.tr: Trong một thí nghiệm thực địa nổi tiếng với danh mục quần áo nữ, cùng một chiếc váy bán chạy hơn ở mức $39 so với $34 hoặc $44.

segments.src: The 9-ending outsold even a *lower* price.
segments.tr: Mức giá kết thúc bằng 9 thậm chí còn bán chạy hơn một mức giá *thấp hơn*.

segments.src: That said, 9-endings are not magic.
segments.tr: Tuy vậy, giá kết thúc bằng 9 không phải là phép màu.

segments.src: Luxury and premium brands often prefer round numbers ($200, not $199.99) precisely because round prices signal quality rather than bargain.
segments.tr: Các thương hiệu xa xỉ và cao cấp thường ưa dùng số tròn ($200, không phải $199.99) chính vì giá tròn truyền tải chất lượng chứ không phải hàng giảm giá.

segments.src: Discount perception: framing the savings**
segments.tr: Cảm nhận về giảm giá: cách trình bày số tiền tiết kiệm**

segments.src: The same discount can be described in different ways, and the description matters.
segments.tr: Cùng một khoản giảm giá có thể được mô tả theo nhiều cách khác nhau, và cách mô tả đó quan trọng.

segments.src: - **Percent vs. dollars:** For cheaper items, a percentage often looks bigger ("25% off" a $12 item sounds better than "$3 off"). For expensive items, the dollar figure often looks bigger ("$300 off" a $1,500 laptop sounds better than "20% off"). Marketers sometimes call this the "rule of 100": below $100, show the percent; above $100, show the dollars. It's a useful rule of thumb, not a law.
segments.tr: - **Phần trăm và số tiền:** Với hàng rẻ, con số phần trăm thường trông lớn hơn ("giảm 25%" cho món $12 nghe hấp dẫn hơn "giảm $3"). Với hàng đắt, con số tiền thường trông lớn hơn ("giảm $300" cho chiếc laptop $1,500 nghe hấp dẫn hơn "giảm 20%"). Giới tiếp thị đôi khi gọi đây là "quy tắc 100": dưới $100, hiển thị phần trăm; trên $100, hiển thị số tiền. Đây là một quy tắc ngón tay cái hữu ích, không phải định luật.

segments.src: - **Relative savings:** People will drive across town to save $10 on a $30 item but often won't for $10 off a $1,000 item, even though the savings are identical. We tend to judge savings as a proportion of the price, not in absolute dollars.
segments.tr: - **Tiết kiệm tương đối:** Người ta sẵn sàng đi xuyên thành phố để tiết kiệm $10 trên món hàng $30 nhưng thường không làm vậy để được giảm $10 trên món $1,000, dù số tiền tiết kiệm như nhau. Chúng ta có xu hướng đánh giá mức tiết kiệm theo tỷ lệ trên giá, chứ không theo số tiền tuyệt đối.

segments.src: In 2012, **JCPenney** tried to simplify its pricing.
segments.tr: Năm 2012, **JCPenney** đã cố gắng đơn giản hóa cách định giá.

segments.src: Instead of marking items up and then running constant sales and coupons, it moved to "fair and square" everyday prices that were often similar to what shoppers had been paying after discounts anyway.
segments.tr: Thay vì đánh dấu giá lên rồi liên tục tổ chức giảm giá và phát phiếu khuyến mãi, hãng chuyển sang mức giá hằng ngày "công bằng và minh bạch", thường gần bằng mức mà khách hàng vốn trả sau khi giảm giá.

segments.src: On paper, customers weren't losing money.
segments.tr: Trên giấy tờ, khách hàng không mất tiền.

segments.src: But they lost the "Was $50, now $29.99" comparison, and with it the feeling of winning a deal.
segments.tr: Nhưng họ mất phép so sánh "Giá cũ $50, nay còn $29.99", và cùng với nó là cảm giác chiến thắng một món hời.

segments.src: Sales fell sharply, the CEO behind the change was replaced in 2013, and the company brought back its sales and coupons.
segments.tr: Doanh số giảm mạnh, CEO đứng sau thay đổi bị thay thế vào năm 2013, và công ty đã khôi phục các đợt bán hàng cùng phiếu giảm giá.

segments.src: You can see the same psychology on any weekend at Target, Walmart, or on Amazon: a crossed-out "List Price," a "Save 30%" badge, or a $29.99 tag sitting next to a $49.99 "premium" version.
segments.tr: Bạn có thể thấy đúng tâm lý này vào bất kỳ cuối tuần nào tại Target, Walmart hay Amazon: một "Giá niêm yết" bị gạch ngang, huy hiệu "Tiết kiệm 30%", hay nhãn $29.99 đặt cạnh phiên bản "cao cấp" $49.99.

segments.src: Each one is designed to give you a reference point that makes the price in front of you look reasonable.
segments.tr: Mỗi thứ đều được thiết kế để tạo ra một điểm tham chiếu khiến mức giá trước mắt bạn trông hợp lý.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. We judge prices against a **reference price**, either remembered (internal) or shown by the seller (external), so context can make the same price feel cheap or expensive.
segments.tr: 1. Chúng ta đánh giá giá dựa trên **giá tham chiếu**, hoặc được ghi nhớ (nội tại) hoặc do người bán đưa ra (bên ngoài), nên bối cảnh có thể khiến cùng một mức giá trông rẻ hoặc đắt.

segments.src: 2. Prices ending in 9 work partly because of the **left-digit effect** and partly because shoppers link them with sales; round prices tend to signal quality instead.
segments.tr: 2. Giá kết thúc bằng 9 hiệu quả một phần nhờ **hiệu ứng chữ số đầu**, và một phần vì người mua liên hệ chúng với khuyến mãi; giá tròn thường truyền tải chất lượng thay thế.

segments.src: 3. How a **discount** is framed (percent vs. dollars, relative vs. absolute savings) changes how big it feels, even when the money saved is the same.
segments.tr: 3. Cách **giảm giá** được trình bày (phần trăm so với số tiền, tiết kiệm tương đối so với tuyệt đối) làm thay đổi cảm nhận về độ lớn của nó, ngay cả khi số tiền tiết kiệm được là như nhau.

segments.src: ## 📚 Key Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ chính

segments.src: - **Reference price:** The benchmark a shopper uses to decide whether a price is high, low, or fair.
segments.tr: - **Giá tham chiếu:** Mốc mà người mua dùng để quyết định một mức giá cao, thấp hay hợp lý.

segments.src: - **Internal reference price:** A benchmark stored in memory, based on past purchases, expectations, or what feels "normal."
segments.tr: - **Giá tham chiếu nội tại:** Mốc được lưu trong trí nhớ, dựa trên các lần mua trước, kỳ vọng hoặc điều được cho là "bình thường".

segments.src: - **External reference price:** A benchmark supplied at the point of sale, such as a "Was" price, MSRP, or a nearby comparison product.
segments.tr: - **Giá tham chiếu bên ngoài:** Mốc được cung cấp tại điểm bán, chẳng hạn giá "Giá cũ", MSRP hoặc một sản phẩm so sánh gần đó.

segments.src: - **Left-digit effect:** The tendency to focus on a price's first digit, so $2.99 feels noticeably cheaper than $3.00.
segments.tr: - **Hiệu ứng chữ số đầu:** Xu hướng tập trung vào chữ số đầu tiên của giá, nên $2.99 có vẻ rẻ hơn rõ rệt so với $3.00.

segments.src: - **Anchoring:** The tendency for an initial number to pull later judgments toward it.
segments.tr: - **Neo giá (Anchoring):** Xu hướng một con số ban đầu kéo các đánh giá sau đó về phía nó.

segments.tr: *Đáp án: Q1 (b).

segments.src: The seller is supplying the comparison point, so it's an external reference price; an internal one would come from your own memory.
segments.tr: Người bán cung cấp điểm so sánh nên đây là giá tham chiếu bên ngoài; giá tham chiếu nội tại sẽ đến từ trí nhớ của chính bạn.

segments.src: Going from $4.00 to $3.99 changes the leftmost digit (4 → 3), which is where the effect is strongest; $4.50 to $4.49 keeps the leftmost digit the same.
segments.tr: Đổi từ $4.00 sang $3.99 làm thay đổi chữ số ngoài cùng bên trái (4 → 3), đây là nơi hiệu ứng mạnh nhất; còn $4.50 sang $4.49 giữ nguyên chữ số ngoài cùng bên trái.

segments.src: For items above roughly $100, the dollar amount ($180) is usually a bigger, more impressive-looking number than the percentage (15%), even though they describe the same discount.*
segments.tr: Với các món trên khoảng $100, số tiền ($180) thường là con số lớn hơn và trông ấn tượng hơn so với phần trăm (15%), dù cả hai đều mô tả cùng một khoản giảm giá.*
